DEMO EVENTS
    Two schematic operations, not an assumed shared footprint. ≈60 AMRs total; the rendered 40 / 20 distribution is visual only. CAD, allocation, routes and timings await validation.Process details & open questions ↗

    Model basis

    Reported equipment

    • Approximately 60 AMRs across the site; allocation between operations is unknown.
    • 14 Yaskawa cobots; 6 ACS; 6 AGS; 15 RATA; 10 RADI.
    • ASRS, KNAPP conveyors, RF and extended testers, and automated packaging. Quantities for these systems were not supplied.
    • Apple, Google, Samsung, Motorola and OnePlus devices.

    What is schematic

    • The relative placement and adjacency of the two operations, orientation, distances and equipment footprints.
    • The 40 / 20 visual AMR split and placement of the fourteen arms on a common transfer row.
    • Cell assignment, routing, chamber loading, ASRS bays, packaging modules and representative manual work.
    • Device arrivals, queue limits, resource slots, travel speed and processing durations are presentation choreography.

    Example routes

    Automated flow, manual fallback / VAS, and repair / retest are deliberately selectable demonstration profiles. Smart receive → hospital receiving is confirmed. Subsequent hospital re-entry, RATA versus RADI eligibility, extended-test sequence, repair return to RF, audit placement and VAS diversion are not yet validated. No inference about brand-specific processing is made.

    Before a predictive model

    Supply reverse and forward CAD files, station allocations, actual route and eligibility matrices, carrier identities, cycle-time distributions, queue capacities, resources and shifts, failure/recovery records, and validation traces. Unknown operating parameters remain unset in the source specification.

    Controls change this animation only. Displayed device-state counts describe the scene and are not operational KPIs or measured performance.
